site.name: Barker No. 3
overview: Barker No. 3 is a documented historic tungsten mine west of Nederland. USGS records describe nearly 1,000 feet of underground workings and about 1,250 units of WO3 production, tying the mapped locality directly to the Boulder County tungsten boom.

timeline.text: State mine-production records cited by the USGS show that Barker No. 3 was producing tungsten during the World War I boom, with about 1,249 units of WO3 recorded for that period.
The mine was worked intermittently after the wartime boom, as operators continued to pursue the Barker vein system.
Wartime redevelopment resumed under lease after the mine had filled with water. USGS reporting traced the old workings, but no production was reported during this campaign.

moreHistory: USGS Professional Paper 245 places Barker No. 3 roughly half a mile west of Nederland and describes a 265-foot shaft with four principal levels and nearly 1,000 feet of workings.
The Barker veins follow the Barker fault zone near the country-rock contact. Historical records document the property as a real tungsten producer, not merely a mapped prospect.

The present Remnant marker uses the documented mapped mine locality at approximately 39.9619, -105.5281. It should be treated as a mine-level historical anchor rather than a claim that a surviving shaft collar has been field-surveyed.
